senses.gloss: m. (פִּיס) division, (cmp. פּוּר, a. בָּצַע) compromise, arbitration, esp. by counting out a certain number on the raised fingers of those among whom a decision is to be made (v. צָבַע Hif.), allotment.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 2:2">Yoma II, 2</cite> <he>התקינו … אלא בפ׳</he> it was ordained that the cleansing of the altar should not be done (by whosoever was the first to reach it) but according to arbitration by counting &c.

<cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 2:2">Ib.</cite> <he>וזה הפ׳ הראשון</he> and this was the first arbitration (on the Day of Atonement). Ib. 3 <he>הפ׳ השני מי וכ׳</he> the second count was to decide who was to slaughter &c.; a. fr.—Pl. <he>פְּיָיסוֹת</he>. Ib. 2 <he>ארבע פ׳ היו שם</he> four times arbitration took place there (on the Day of Atonement).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 6:1:18">Y. Pes. VI, 33ᵇ</cite> <he>מפני קילקול פ׳</he> because it disturbs the arrangement of the various services allotted severally to the priests; a. e.
